target_questions.question: Does exit cross-section shape reorganize shock topology and radial mixing independently of pressure ratio?
target_questions.target_basis: Tier 1 B028 identifies nozzle diameter as a mixing control; this study extends geometry to non-axisymmetric shapes.

evidence_candidates.claim_text: Non-axisymmetric hydrogen-jet exit shapes generate different shock systems and nonuniform radial expansion, with axis switching and mixing/penetration differences correlated with boundary vorticity.
evidence_candidates.evidence_summary: Triangular, star, elliptical, and rectangular sections are compared under a common numerical framework.

core_links.shared_parameter_or_mechanism: nozzle geometry controls shear-layer growth and mixing

limitations: Numerical free-jet configurations; shape and aspect-ratio effects are coupled.
visual_verification: Targeted visual verification performed where numeric/glyph-dependent abstract claims required it; no figure digitization.
